title: I Converted From Electric to Gas
text:
Our house has gas heating and hot water. Fortunately, it was also plumbed for a gas oven/cook top. This unit just dropped right into my existing 30" wide opening. I had to purchase a flexible gas line and find a 120v electric source since the previous range was 240v with no common wire. I tapped into one of the backsplash appliance outlets and ran a new outlet in the cabinet below.

Something they don't mention is that the cook top comes with feet on it so you can actually set it on a flat surface if you are going portable and using propane.

The only downside is that the instructions are terrible. They assume a lot and actually have incomplete directions where they appear to try. No hook-up diagram about the gas line. I looked up how to videos online and got all my answers there. It WAS easy to install but minus one star for the acute lack of proper paperwork and not a word about converting from another type of cook top. They did provide a full-size cardboard template for the hole and that helped me know it would fit.

NOTE: you need to have an exhaust hood equal to 1% of the total BTU output of the range. I have the 5-burner and adding it all up, that was 37,000 BTU, so a 370 CFM would be appropriate. It also needs to be 24" above the countertop and mine was just a little lower and built into a microwave. I looked up the microwave specs and it is rated to go above a gas cook top.

Now I know how those TV cooking shows produce food so fast. I hardly have to wait for the pan to heat up before I am flipping eggs. Much faster than before and the heat seems to be more even across the pan. The wife and I are looking forward to a new era of cooking and if the power goes out - we can still cook meals!

title: Fit,color, and price couldn't ask for better!
text: Packaging is different than it's pictured but I am not buying it for the clear plastic bag with a place for shelf hanger punched into it. The packaging is fairly protective yet easily able to opened by most anyone. Each item was individually packaged in a appropriate size box and the boxes were then placed into a thin plastic Amazon shipping bag. The products color is perfectly matched as well as the shape being identical to the originals that came with the fridge/freezer originally. The only apparent difference I notice is in the stiffness of the plastic with the plastic being slightly more ridged than the original ones. This flexibility may not present itself as being a problem at all but in my past experience with plastics as a rule of thumb (yes I do know the origin of the rule) they tend to have a propencity of becoming increasingly more brittle as temperatures decrease. This product is made for use in a freezer (which most of us attempt to keep them cold)  so if it does become extremely brittle that would be unexceptable in my opinion. Our staff (my wife, 3 kids, 4 dogs, and myself) is feverishly working around the clock rigorously preforming extream durability tests to insure that they stand up to even the  harshest most grueling abuse known to man (😜). If any incident or less than ideal results are gathered through our testing our results shall be posted and our review will be altered to reflect the data gathered at that time. I don't often take the time to write reviews but felt that after seeing the product I received I made an exception deeming it to be deserving of my time. I personally have a tendency to be hesitant and usually pass on purchasing a product that has shipping costs involved and especially if it has yet to be reviewed. They seem to be well above average quality control, (that in my experience is unheard of when it comes budget manufacturering from around the world) decent quality and an excellent value so I hope that if you are skeptical or leary of purchasing any aftermarket part that this may help to alleviate some of the concern for this particular product. If the seller is reading this and values my opinion I would like to point out that you are providing a good product at a great price (which very much seems to be the case barring temperature causing your product to become ridiculously brittle or other unforseen defects occurring) If you are able to take the costs of shipping and in some way include it in price I see when I look in my basket to make it easier for us to compare prices that would be appreciated and may lead to more sales. I am going to guess that I am not the only shopper that tends not to add items with shipping to my shopping cart (the first rounds of cuts) because the cost is aperent unless you go through with a fine tooth comb and make your own total of each product. The other reason that I tend to avoid items that have a additional shipping charges is because I think to myself they must not be confident in the product that they sell and when It gets it here and in my hands for a closer look I will see that it is trash.  If I decide that it is going to be returned I get stuck with another charge to return the item or I deem that it is not worth returning because the hassle and/or fee involved you get a person who isn't happy and many times they have a tendency to tell many others about the negative experience with your product and sometimes even take to attempting to smear the company that you have worked very hard to start. Many times the new products and companies show up here on Amazon from different countries and they aren't aware of the different challenges of other societal practices and how these practices are viewed. Sometimes things that would be abused and cause great amount of cost and lost profits can be a cost of doing business in another cultures market. Sadly many times it will end up in bankruptcy and without them even being aware of the fact that they are expected to accommodate the practice and it needs to be budgeted into the costs involved.

title: Replacement parts arrived quickly
text:
My Whirlpool dryer stopped heating, so while I was looking for a new element, I came across this package and decided that I might as well replace everything while I had the back off. For the price of the kit, it's pretty much a no-brainer.

Got my package the next day, but it was only the element, so I asked for a replacement. It arrived two days later, so I pulled the dryer out of its cubby and replaced everything. It was pretty quick to complete. Took longer to get the dryer to a place where I could work on it than it took to replace everything.

I started it up, element glowed and was getting nice hot air out of the vent, so I called it done and put it back together and maneuvered it back in place. That's when the problems started. It ran for a little bit and then stopped tumbling and the dryer got really hot, so I turned it off. After it cooled, I pulled it back out and discovered that the thermal fuse did its job and shut it down. Luckily I still had the old thermal fuse, so I put it back in place. I checked all the thermostats and the element for continuity and they all were good, so I plugged back in and ran it. It heated back up and seemed to be doing good, until the high limit thermostat cut the power to the element and I noticed that only half of the element shut off. That's not what it's supposed to do. I turned on the air dry cycle that uses no heat, only air and I noticed that the same side of the element heated up. That's when I knew I had a problem.

The one thing I didn't check before I put everything in place was for continuity between the element and its cover. Sure enough, it was bad. Looks like one or more of the insulators on that side was not working properly and it was getting juice as soon as the dryer was turned on.

Luckily, I had been lazy and hadn't returned the other original element that I had received, so I checked it and it was good and put it on. Problem solved and I have a working dryer again.

Long story short, when you check the element, make sure you check for continuity between the posts and between the post and element case itself. That will help save you any headaches later on.

The element that I am putting back in the return box has obviously been used, so I am putting a note in the box to let the seller know why it's been used. Hopefully they won't charge me for element. If they do, I'll update this post with my observations about their customer service.

title: Great for monitoring humidity inside.
text: I got this to help me monitor humidity changes that I thought may be affecting migraine episodes. It reads humidity well. It was relatively easy to figure out how to set up the "if-then" alerts but the option was very limited. I wanted to set it up to alert me if humidity rose or dropped by x% in a specific period of time so I could track if my symptoms occur on rising or falling humidity and hopefully get ahead of when they would occur. I was limited to <=> temp and either humidity dry, comfortable or moist. I will have to put some time in to figure out what combinations will give me the information I was looking for. I quickly disabled the alerts because the app was alerting nearly constantly. When I cleared the push notification, it would alert again minutes later. It is nice that the app shows the readings throughout the day so you can tell if humidity was rising or falling when you experienced a migraine syndrome symptom. All in all, the monitor is good and the app could be better.  If you just need to be able to check humidity it's a great product. If you have something that depends on consistent humidity, be prepared to configure multiple alerts to achieve the goal of monitoring % change. Recommended!

title: Is water leaking from the top of your coffee maker?
text: We've had our coffee maker since May 2019.  Love it, I use the filter to use my own grind.  About a week ago water started leaking from the top.  I tried a pod, same thing.  It was like more water was going in than was coming out the bottom, and it started doing this suddenly.  Upon close examination I noticed that the brochure picture on the web site showed a small grommet that was missing on mine.  The grommet would form a tight seal against the pod or the reusable filter cup.  I was lucky and found mine under the drying rack for my reusable filter cup.  If your machine leaks water from the top, check for that grommet, if its missing, that's your problem.  If you can't buy a replacement find a Vet, they should be able to Jerry-rig something for you, to keep you in the fight.

I installed it somewhere i dont plan to move it around, but i could imagine picking it up and moving it occasionally. Despite its size, its not that heavy.

Also the spin cycle is very good, not a single one of my loads drips when i remove it.

When i first recieved it, i had a large backlog of laundry to do, and ran it almost non-stop for 2 days, and the last wash was as good as the first.

Don't walk away from this machine.....RUN! Run Fast and run far.

Nothing works on this. Had unit set to vent when drying. 5 1/2 hours of drying, and clothes were nothing but a steaming hot wet mess. Dryer was set to vent mode and dryer vent hose was straight (no twists, turns or bends) and was less than 12 inches in length. I actually relocated the dryer vent to meet the exhaust port on the unit directly. Still nothing would dry. There is a small fan where the dryer vent hose connects and that is the only way to remove the hot and moist air when drying. Fan does not move air at all. Don't believe when they say the fan "shoots air up to 50 feet". This fan could not move air 12 inches.

When checking machine why it would not dry it was found that while drying, the machine would continually shoot water into the tub causing clothes to just be steaming hot soaked mess. When checking the machine, I mistakenly put my hand on the right side of the unit and burned my hand! Got my temperature reader out and gauged the side of the machine at 133.1 degrees! This was the OUTSIDE of the machine. I can't imagine what the temperature of the internal components were. This is a major fire hazard and safety issue. Skin suffers 2nd degree burns at 131 degrees.

Called manufacturer to complain. Was told they needed to send out a service tech and they needed 2 to 3 days to find a repair company. After one day they called to give me the contact information for a repair company to call and schedule a warranty repair. Called this company for 3 days trying to set something up and never once received a call back. Called manufacturer again and was told I had to keep trying. This was the company I had to use. Finally was able to convince the manager at the store where I purchased this unit to allow me to return for a different brand. DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT.

text:
Unfortunately, I can't write about the performance of this washer. This is a digital display, compact, fully automatic washer. When I received it, it looked very nice, well built and had a good amount of weight to it.... Plus, it is cute as heck! It has a stainless steel spinner and it is perfect for small spaces and would do about half a normal sized load of laundry.
Unfortunately, I wasn't able to use it. My intention was to use it in the bathroom, but I had no way to adapt it to the faucet in my bathroom, or in my kitchen. Something to keep in mind if you're going to use it in your bathroom, or kitchen: Make sure you have a way to adapt the hose to a faucet or washer hookup. It also needs to be filled through the water inlet (a shower head or bucket can't be used) and the water pressure has to be at a certain rate or it will not sense that there's water in it and it won't agitate. Because of that and poor water pressure in my bathroom, it wasn't going to work for me. I returned it and purchased something that works.

title: Actually works very well
text:
This thing is tall and takes up a good amount of space in the fridge (and it did not fit in my door shelves at all), but it's worth it because it actually WORKS. We have rabbits and need to keep copious amount of cilantro and dill for them and this has made it so easy. I can fit between 2-3 rather large bundles of cilantro in this at once.

I prewash the herbs and then stick them in here and they've stayed as good as new for 2 weeks (maybe longer but always use them up before then). Compared to leaving herbs in the bag, well, there is no comparison. They barely last at all that way.

When I pack it to the max it's not the easiest to open and close it, but even so it's certainly not hard to do either. I just smush it all in and down. They're just fine in there.

And when I've used everything up it's super simple, quick and easy to clean. Just a good rinsing and wiping down with a paper towel and it's good to go again. So it saves me a bunch of time, money and effort. Really it's a win/win/win. I would recommend it. Hope this helps!

title: Perfect little fridge for perishables
text:
This small fridge is perfect for storing a moderate quantity of perishables at a convenient location
+ Quite light and easy to transport, yet has reasonable insulation and power efficiency. In terms of noise it is virtually silent
+ Big enough to store gallon jugs if the shelves are rearranged
+ While the fridge follows a common design of having a freezer tray on the top and a less cool area for general storage, the whole fridge can be used as freezer when set to the coolest setting
The power consumption of this fridge is 70W when the compressor is on. In a 71F room with the power set to maximum/ coolest (7 on the dial), I measured the following temperatures with my IR thermometer: The freezer tray surface cooled down to -15F. A mug with water on the middle shelf froze to 30F after 3 hours.

title: Misunderstanding what these filters do
text: I read a bunch of reviews on this filter and filters in general.  There seems to be a lot of confusion as to what they are supposed to do and why some cost so much more than other models.  First of all... these are FILTERS... they do not reduce dissolved solid in the water, they reduce or eliminate chemical and biological contaminants.  One person showed how she tested 3 glasses of water with a conductivity meter to show that this filter doesn't do anything.  They DO NOT nor are they SUPPOSED to reduce dissolved solids.  If you want to drink water with zero dissolved solids, then drink distilled water... at least until you wind up in the hospital, because of it.  The difference in cost is directly related to how much and what chemicals/biologics are removed from the water.  Cheap ones are basically activated charcoal which gets rid of some things like chlorine and foul tasking water.  More expensive ones will filter out or reduce dozens and dozens of chemicals and biologics.  If you don't know what your water contains you can contact your local water source (city, village etc.) and they can provide you a list of contaminants in your water.  I typically buy those that will reduce as many contaminants as possible... 66 to 73.  They cost about $10 more, but the peace of mind is worth the small additional cost.

text: These stove gap covers do a decent job of covering the unsightly gap between the counter and range so that food doesn't fall down into an inaccessible crevasse.  The shiny black metal looks nice next to my shiny black cooktop, but the design doesn't work that well with my wood counters, which have a tongue-and-groove stepped-back edge that isn't squared off.  Perhaps for that reason, these stove gap covers always work their way upwards, and I'm constantly poking them down to try and get them to lie flat along the top of the counter edge.  The bad part about that is that food gets stuck under the covers, especially when my kids cook (see photos).  It's not that easy to yank these up and remove them to clean underneath, but at least the food doesn't fall away to floor level where it's virtually impossible to clean regularly.  However, I'm a bit disappointed by the performance of these covers over the past few months because they are so fiddly.  They were a bit on the pricey side for an almost-right solution to the stove gap problem, but I'm giving them four stars because after several months of hard use (we use the stove to cook a LOT every day), they still look just as nice as the day I installed them, and they're very easy to clean with a damp sponge.

title: An Important Thing To Know
text: If you've ever had to replace an electric stove element, you will be aware that there are two types of connectors: blades or loops. These two types of connectors are usually NOT interchangeable. I have Hotpoint range that takes loops. When I received this element it had blades, but as the 'Amazon Confirmed Fit' tool said it was compatible with my model, I installed it. Worked perfectly! Just so you know. I will note that the coil is truly flat (not semi-rounded like on cheaper elements) and gives you more surface area for heating. It also sits flush in the drip pan unlike the cheaper models. It's a pricey element, but if you have the money, worth it.

Ordered this ice machine for using in my game room without having to go up/down the stairs to my kitchen for iced water. It makes large and small size ice nuggets, and makes 9 ice cubes in under 10 minutes! I keep a 5 gallon jug of filtered water upstairs for refilling the ice machine, I have never used tap water. The unit is quiet (barely louder than a bathroom fan) and has a decent sized, removable basin for holding ice and a deep water reservoir. If you don't use the ice and it stacks up, there's a sensor that stops the machine from making more ice (or until it melts down), so you don't have to worry about overfill, ever.

I have a very short list of pro's and con's:

PRO'S:
+ Quickly makes ice (just let it cycle filtered water and dispose the first round per directions)
+ Two sizes for ice cubes which can be selected on the top
+ Never overfills and will automatically stop when tray is full of ice
+ Conveniently quiet, no louder than a bathroom fan, and never beeps
+ Very mobile, would be great for tailgating or camping with electric plugs
+ Does not produce a lot of heat in a confined area (but make sure it's ventilated)
+ Convenient removable ice tray and nice hand scoop provided

CON'S:
- Takes a couple of hours for a full ice tray
- Can't use tap water, must be filtered (just read the directions)
- Initial set up takes a full day to run water through the maker before regular use
- Ice cubes are not very big, so they can melt quickly in room temp liquids
- Ice cubes are tube shaped, not chipped or nugget style
- Plastic parts do feel flimsy, so take care to not use too roughly

I hope this review helps potential buyers. I was very, very hesitant but now I use it more than my kitchen fridge! Very happy customer.

title: A good, portable, induction one-burner but no safety certification
text:
My wife and I have been using a 4-burner induction cooktop for over 10 years. We love it. But sometimes, we've needed an extra burner, and this unit pretty-much fills the bill.

If you're new to induction cooking, it's responsive, like cooking with natural gas. It's also energy-efficient, which is why you can have one- or even two-burner portable units running on a 110V outlet. Best of all, it works well with inexpensive steel/iron cookware. That brings us to the one caveat of induction cooking: if a magnet won't stick to your pan, it won't work on an induction burner. Happily, you'll find the most inexpensive cookware is generally made of steel and will work great, but take a magnet with you when you go shopping.

We tested our unit with a watt-meter and found the unit's performance was dependent on the size of the pan. A six-inch diameter pan on high-heat drew 1320 watts while an eight-inch pan took 1700 watts. Using the 8-inch pan, it took 2:45 minutes to boil a pint of water. That's not bad; a unit on our 220V built-in took 1:50 to perform the same task. Using a seven-inch pan on high-heat, the unit got 4 TBS of olive oil to 470°F in well under 30 seconds. Unhappily, the unit draws 3 watts when plugged-in but off.

The fan is a bit loud. It's tolerable in moderate use, but gets annoying in a 4-hr simmer. It starts when the unit is powered-on and auto-shuts-off one minute after the unit is turned off. We don't understand the focus on watts/temperature in the display. Neither are very accurate. Frankly, just displaying 1-10 for power level would be more meaningful to most of us in the US.

My one big concern: the unit doesn't show any safety certification -- no UL (USA), CE (EU), or even EMC badge. Not on the product itself, in the User Manual, on the packing box, or anywhere on-line. In this day and age, I find this inexcusable. Maybe it's a packaging oversight, maybe the manufacturer forgot to get it tested, or maybe it was tested and failed safety certification. How are we to know? But without that certification, use at your own risk.

title: This has fixed the Samsung Refrigerator FreezeUp Isssue! You can fix yours too!
text:
I was getting pretty good at defrosting the back panel of my Samsung Refrigerator. Had plenty of practice, probably did it 5 times, maybe every 2 or 3 months for a while there. Each time I thought I'd fixed it forever. Samsung refrigerators have a real issue, the rear panel, behind it, collects ice. That's where the cooling coils are. Eventually the ice messes with the airflow, messes with the fan, so the Refrigerator stops cooling well.

There are several good videos on youtube, you can probably find one on your exact model. It'll show you how to remove the stuff you need to to get access for this fix. You need to get to and remove the back panel.

A few notes,... get some coolers and towels to protect your cold stuff. It'll be hours before your frig is cold again. Figure out the controls so you can do a power cool when you start it up again. If you have two hair driers that's best you'll need to defrost the back panel, likely it's bonded with the ice that collected on the cooling coils. Alternating hair driers is best they really aren't made to run for more than about 5 minutes Mine quit from an overheating safety lock. So heat up the back panel, and blow warm air into the vents. Evidently the panel will start to loosen, don't force it. I believe it was most of 30 minutes of blowing. The ice also contains some wires that you don't want to destroy by forcing things early, you also don't want to stress the cooling coils. Take your time with the hair dryers. Eventually you can separate the edges and get more air back there. The melted ice will go everywhere, so have plenty of towels. When it actually separates be careful because there are some wires that you'll need to be careful not to stress, on mine you can turn the back, rotate it, so that you can get at the connectors upper left. Make sure you carefully disconnect the wires, noting where they go, ...pictures are in order. I had to prop things up while I finished the defrost in that area. Once you've removed the back panel by disconnecting the wires. finish defrosting everything, ice on mine was everywhere.

There really aren't instructions that come with the kit, but there are plenty of you tube videos to show you what you're doing.

This kit is great, I haven't had any issues for most of a year, once I did the fix. At one time I had the ECO mode enabled, turn that off, it' suppresses the defroster which you need working. It's just not worth it to save a buck on power but have your frig freeze up repeatedly. The odd metal thing in the kit has a tongue that is inserted into the drain hole at the bottom of the coils, clip it on the defrosters heating element, it transfers the heat from the defroster to keep the drain hole open, works great, make sure you bend the two smaller tongues around the heating element so that it has better contact so it can melt more ice.

The other helpful item is the thermal sensor. It should be moved, the youtube videos highlight that it was originally in the wrong place. I can't swear that my old one was bad, but it's not worth doing this again, just get the kit and stick the sensor in the improved location, if I recall it was in the same area but over a cooling tube. It may be that the sensor is a bit improved, it looks a bit different, has longer wires, but from my experience it works. I think I read that somebody got a bad one, that's why I got the dual kit. I checked them with an ohmmeter and mine were both fine.

One of the videos also suggested that you seal up the airflow around the coils, I didn't mess with that, it didn't seem like it would make a large difference to me.

I was about ready to trash my expensive Samsung refrigerator I was so unhappy with it. But now I think its back in business, the ice buildup issue is now gone. ...has been for most of a year. It seems the new type refrigerators don't last as long averaging only 5 years, my theory is this issue once solved will keep lots of frigs around longer, perhaps much longer.

I think anyone can probably do this fix if you're careful, ...helps to have two people, spend sometime on youtube videos. It uses screw drivers, hair driers, nothing real exotic for tools, I feel like I saved thousands, you can too. Get this kit and learn from my experience, just do it once.

text:
[[VIDEOID:142907a9d94c6de3d373a3f3d9b4d0fa]] This washing system really works! You can see it agitating your laundry just like an electric washing machine! And it's good exercise!

There's something soothing about using this thing. You can develop your own rhythm, and switch over to "high speed wash" anytime you want! Also work smarter- use the "soak" feature and let the water do a lot of the work.

It's not a small washer- it's about the size of an outdoor garbage can. It fits easily in my RV shower and I just take it out to use the shower.

The more water you use the easier it will be to churn your laundry. But you can use the same wash water for several loads, and then dump that out (I put the water in my toilet to help clean out the black tank), and then use the same rinse water a few times over. Just scoop the bubbles of soap off the top, add a little more fresh water, and you can easily do three or four loads w/o starting over with new water each time.

This works best in an RV site with full sewer hookups, so you can just empty the used water in your grey or black tanks. If you are off grid, then there are environment friendly soaps you can buy so that you can dispose of your wash water safely.

I would recommend this for anyone who wants to avoid laundromats. They are so expensive these days!

title: Used for Whirlpool WTW5000DW1
text:
My machine was barely agitating and wasn't spinning and gave me error code F7E5. I thought it was the acuator but that wasn't it. Turns out the sprocket that goes over the spring broke because the widest part of it separated so the piece that connects to the acuator was not engaging preventing the tub from agitating or spinning.

Like others have said the belt is too small. Maybe I could have forced it, but with plastic pieces why chance it when my current belt looked perfectly fine? Also, the piece with the tabs that connects to bottom (in my case it goes in and locks into place by turning it clockwise wouldn't lock into place so I used the old one instead. So of all the pieces the kit came with, I only used two. I used the piece that was broken and the ring with the tab that connects to the actuator arm and bam, worked perfectly. So this solved my problem, but like others have said, it's not nearly a perfect fit for my model.

title: Not designed to work with my Maytag Neptune MAH3000AWW
text:
[[VIDEOID:394f652ad34a3cf73b932693120be840]] This really didn’t work with my Maytag Neptune MAH3000AWW washing machine. The only part of this kit that was of any use was the 10” punch. I used the punch to drive out the old inner and outer bearings. The PVC tubing was not up to the job of driving out the bearings. The steel disks were not large enough in diameter. When pushing in the new bearings the steel disks should push on the outer bear races. This tool pushed on the inner bearing race or on the bearing plastic side covers. I wound up driving the new bearings in by using the old bearings and pounding on the old bearings as was done in the 2 YouTube videos. Other reviews referred to YouTube videos showing how to use this tool, but I did not find these videos.
There are a lot of reviews saying that this is a must have tool, but those reviews appear to be “Brushings”. A “Brushing” is when you purchase an item and have it sent to some random Amazon customer so that you can write a glowing review of your product.
I could design a better tool.
I made a tool out of a piece 1/2” & 3/4” dia PVC shown in the picture to center the inner stainless steel sleeve between the inner and outer bearings. To center the location of the inner sleeve after both outer bearing races were seated, I used a ball peen hammer and a BFSD (Big F’n Screw Driver) to center the inner sleeve so that the shaft would slide in.
It appears that the reason the bearings started making a lot of noise is because the seal failed because of the non-stainless steel metal used in the bearing seal. I bought this machine new 25 years ago in 1997. Hopefully, it will be good for another 25 years.

title: Portable Ice Factory (But Not For Storage)
text:
It can't get much easier than this to produce ice and a lot of it. The manufacturer recommends letting the unit rest for a day after receiving to allow the refrigerant to settle . While you're letting it rest go ahead and clean everything. Also plan on a place to put it. You'll need space (picture for reference) and power.

Keep in mind this machine is for producing ice, and not storing it long term. Yes this has a bucket built in to catch what it makes but the instructions say not to exceed 18 hours - or they'll melt. Melting isn't totally a lost cause because they melt into the trough and will be recycled. I wouldn't worry about it too much because to keep up with the machine you'll have to empty the bucket way before that anyway. I'd say empty it every few hours on average. If you don't the bucket will fill up and it will automatically stop producing new 'bullets'. It produces 9 large (or small) bullets in roughly 10 minutes which is within it's stated specifications. 54 or so 'bullets' per hour isn't shabby.

As I mentioned this produces 'bullet' shaped cubes either large or small. This is one of my favorite shapes.

Starting the unit is straightforward. Pull out the basket and fill the trough under the basket with water to the max fill line. I recommend using filtered water to avoid any off flavors (this is true no matter what kind of ice maker you have). Replace the basket. Shut the lid. Plug in the unit. Select large or small 'bullets'. Press the start button and you're off to the races. It will keep producing 'bullets' until it runs out of water or fills up the bucket. Status lights tell you what options you've selected and what it's up to.

Instructions are included for cleaning. Essentially hand clean everything removable (basket, scoop, measuring cup), use the clean cycle and a vinegar solution to clean everything else. There is a drain plug in the bottom front.

The on/off for this unit is plugging it into an outlet. There is no power switch but there is a pause function. If you press pause the unit will eject whatever ice it currently is in the process of freezing. So you might as well wait until you hear it complete a freeze cycle and then press pause.

I'd suggest using this in the day(s) leading up to a party or some other function. It cranks out the ice and you're assured to have plenty when you need it.

title: So glad I got this!!
text:
I picked this machine as a Christmas gift for my husband after our 9yr old keurig could not be cleaned to my liking anymore. I read a TON of reviews for this machine, and others, before picking it. And I'm so glad I did.

Other reviews:
One guy said his coffee (beans and fluid) spilled all over, making a huge mess, in the enclosed pod space. But another reviewer mentioned you do have to push the kcup down in place in this machine (you don't have to in the keurig). She was right and there is no mess, no overflow.
One review mentioned the blue led screen was so bright.... I worried it would be too bright and make my kitchen glow blue, but it's not too bright at all.
A few mentioned that it splatters on itself while dripping. This is true, but it's VERY EASY to wipe off, no cleaning supplies needed. Don't you wipe your machine down once in awhile anyway..?

What we love:
The led screen is nice, it tells you what you need to do, it's easy to use, I love it.
There are several size options, and it does save your preferences, you don't have to pick every time.
It starts up instantly, no warm up required before pouring.
It's smaller than the keurig, less bulky, and takes up less space
We use the "hot water" option every night, to make tea, love this option!

What we don't love:
His travel mug doesn't fit, so we use a regular mug and pour it into his travel mug every day.
The "hottest" setting is not as hot as the keurigs single, default setting, and he likes his coffee HOT.
The strength is not as strong, but this is a taste preference (you can just use a smaller oz setting and use 2 pods)
The clock itself does not light up, it's dark on the light up screen. So when the machine is off, can't see the clock :(

Overall:
Very attractive, easy to use, easy to clean machine. No problems with it working (it's been 5 months). I would recommend this, and I would buy it again!

title: It silenced my screeching dryer
text:
My Maytag Maxima dryer was screeching horribly. It would typically screech for a solid minute or two when starting a cycle, and then it would quiet down. I had had enough.

The interwebs suggested I could crack open the dryer to expose the innards and then simply clean and lubricate the rollers and pulley. I tried that, and it improved things significantly, but the screeching wasn't completely gone. From taking things apart, I knew the tensioner pulley was the main problem, but I ordered the whole kit to refresh everything. Now that stubborn screech is gone!

The triangle clips are a pain to deal with. You can cut the old ones off, but you still have to be careful installing the new ones, so you don't break them. I found that heating the clips in hot water for several minutes increased their flexibility and made them a little easier to work with. They were still a pain, but I got progressively faster installing each one.

Since I was already down to the machine's guts, I used a shop vac to clean up 10 years of lint, while wondering to myself why all this lint had never burned my house down.

My fingers are sore from installing the triangle clips, but my dryer is quiet (and clean) once again.

title: A New Way To Wash Dishes
text:
This little dishwasher is really something. I was skeptical about it at first, thinking there was no way something so small have not only the power to wash but dry and sanitize.
So here's my rundown:

The Pros:
1. It's small. It's less than the width of a microwave, but slightly taller, just about as deep. It will fit almost anywhere. Just less than 18 inches high, I found it could fit on a side counter between the fridge and sink itself, or under cabinets next to the sink.
2. Dual filling means that you can either add hot water to the machine yourself or if your sink has a removable aerator, you can use the included faucet hose to connect (make sure you REALLY snap the hose to adapter well) your existing hot water to the machine and never worry about filling again.
3. Has a removable silverwear tray, removable dish rack with fold down dish holding arms, and a removable metal mesh and fine particle filter for easy inside cleaning of the machine (yes, its plastic inside so that means grease and oils that dish soap hasn't fully broken down may stick to the plastic) can be removed and manually cleaned daily or weekly depending how often you do dishes.
4. It is INEXPENSIVE. At about $300 the machine more than pays for itself in that it can be used even in the smallest of New York apartments, college dorms or shared housing, apartments and homes in urban areas that were built before dishwashers, or simply you just want a machine that can give your dishes a heat cycle to sanitize them, this really is a steal of a deal.
5. It really cleans! Yep, it has two spinning water arms, one on the top and one on the bottom and the water is pressurized so it comes out as a spray. Not as strong as large dishwashers, so you don't have to worry about dishes flying out of the rack or anything like that, but the water spray will totally remove food from dishes. There either is a water heater or it is very efficient with its use of water and hot drying element because it also has a sanitization cycle that washes baby bottles. And it does dry VERY well.

The Cons:
1. It wont clean extremely caked on food or dishes that have any mold. As in it will wash them like a dishwasher, but it does not have the same temperature settings over 200F nor the extra pressure like a full size dishwasher has. When I say it cleans, I mean, you put your dishes in it the same day and wash them. Overnight will be fine, but it won't get days old dishes clean as well. You may have to pre-wash or double wash.
2. Its all plastic. It might claim to be 40-50lbs but it certainly feels more like 25-30lbs. It doesn't feel "cheap" but it also doesn't feel like it would last more than a few moves. It might last a few years even if used daily but not moved around too much. The plastic inside also means at some point you WILL have to use a degreaser soap (Dawn, Sunlight, etc) to manually clean the inside of any caked on grease or food. It's not that big of a deal, but if it was metal it would be slightly less slick and greasy.
3. LONG dishwashing cycle for the C1 Hygiene, Regular, Glasses type cycles. We are talking over 2 hours each. The difference is 10-20 minutes and the temperature of the drying cycle. There is a rapid cycle that is 40 minutes but lacks any drying cycle so your dishes will still be wet. So this really is one of those machines you gotta maximize your loads and time, overnight loads are great with a heat cycle.
4. Large items WILL NOT FIT. Full size plates are hit or miss. You might fit them in but the upper spin arm may not spin even if they do fit. The medium size plates and bowls and regular size glasses all fit fine. Not really tall containers or water bottles. No pots and pans or lids either. This is okay though because these items really should be washed by hand anyway.

I have so far done about 6 washes over 2 days with the machine and I will say that I'm quite impressed with it. Would definitely recommend to those who are in the market for something small and basic but has features and options and can fit in their homespace or lifestyle. I will also say, make sure you use dishwasher soap that is either powder or tablet as these seem to dissolve slower than liquid so it stays sudsy and has the gritty particles in the water that help scrub plates better than the liquid versions or the included liquid version of Finish. Get the small 96 count Finish tablets, those fit perfect, not too much soap not too little. Make sure to use the hottest water you can either filling manually or by hose. If by hose, run the water to hot prior to reconnecting the hose. Make sure your drain hose is DOWN and has no upward slopes. The pressure to drain is good, but no one likes a backup.

Enjoy your life changing mini dishwasher!

title: Changing original review
text:
Great ice, terrible support.

This unit makes great ice. However, it's very prone to problems. It needs to be cleaned far more frequently than the product support documentation states. Absolutely should be used with a water filter unless your water is impeccably free from sediment or other impurities. The water pump can be loud to very loud--akin to the noise put off by a normal window air conditioner in the room. And these units can run hot--mine did so to the point where it was melting the ice in the bin almost as fast as it was making it.

Support for these devices is terrible. Typical interaction turnaround time with support takes 3-5 days, so they can email you a question or ask you to do something, and if you get back to them right away, it takes another 3-5 days for a response. Then if they agree to send a replacement (refurbished) unit to resolve the problem, they need to get one in stock, which takes several weeks. In my case, I've had a support ticket open for two months now as the replacement unit was louder and had the same overheating problem as my original unit so I sent it back. I would expect far better support for a $500+ appliance.

title: One of the best purchases we ever made!
text:
So my guy and I live in a tiny apartment that is a duplex from a slightly bigger house. We do not have washer and dryer hookups because the bigger part of the duplex has those. We have been using laundrymats for nearly 6 years, so we decided to order a portable washer.
Now my guy is very meticulous in what he chooses to order. He had been looking around Amazon for one that he liked, that had good reviews, and would fit our needs. I started looking and came across this one. I showed it to him and he said it was one that he had looked at as well. We pulled the trigger on the purchase.
OMG! When we got it we did a little load just to see how it went. The hookup was quick and easy. The only complaint I will say was that the washer inlet hose that came with it was... flimsy at best. For a little while, til we could get something that was much more suitable, we simply used a bucket (which does take a min) or the sink sprayer (Which is nice but you have to stand there the whole time) to fill it up.
The washer did not leak, the drain feature worked as it should and the time to wash was crazy fast, even for heavy loads. Some of our clothes needed a second wash but that was not the washer's fault. We were also pleasantly surprised by how little noise it made! Our neighbor goes to sleep early because she works early and we have done laundry late into the night. On the other side of our small apartment, you can barely hear the swish, swish of the washer side, and the spin cycle side spins out EVERYTHING we have put in it with no second spins needed! I even recommended it to a friend who was thinking about getting something for him and his fiancee who are in a similar situation to me and my guy! Highly recommend!
PS: the directions are kinda hard to read, with some bad translations and typos, but you can pretty much get the jest of what to do to get it started.
PPS: the item may come labeled as Costway but a little research showed me that Giantex owns that brand as well.

title: If you don't get a damaged one due to poor shipping you're good to go.
text:
There are many options that came up with my search using the LG part number from the manual, all claiming they were the same part, yet they all looked different. Take the time to look at your motor to ensure it will work. My model has 3 prongs for electrical connections and the metal washer (*don't know the official name) is toward the bottom of the rod, not the top.

I eventually found the right one and watched the price as it fluctuates A LOT. I got mine for $39.

As stated in many reviews, the packaging is awful. The first one arrived damaged. The copper coils were cut and dangling everywhere. Obviously not going to work.

The second one also arrived poorly packaged in a box with the plastic air packs, which were popped as there was nothing else projecting it. I had little hope this would work, but it looked intact, so I tried.

It worked. It was a perfect replacement. I will update if it breaks. Considering the original only lasted < 4 years, I don't have too much hope this will last too long, but I was getting tired of an inconsistent oven with hot spots causing a lot of problems.

The install is extremely easy. The hardest part is taking off all the screws to get to the motor. You also have to unscrew the cover on the inside of the oven. *Helpful note, unscrew the bolt holding the fan blade on the inside of the oven first, before unscrewing the motor on the back. Also, the bolt on the inside fan blade is opposite from conventional wisdom, so turn to the right to loosen. It took me 25 minutes to swap them out and I have zero experience.

So far, for $39 bucks it's a good deal. Hopefully it lasts a long time.

title: Cool New Gadget For The RV
text:
Works Great, some adjustments listed below. Bought to add some additional flavored drink options to the RV. Flavored coffee pods, flavored tea pods, & Hot cocoa pods. If making regular coffee is better to just use aero press & if regular tea, a tea ball is better, however this is perfect for my desired use.
For flavored coffee follow directions. For Flavored Tea (I do chai or cinnamon) push down until some comes out, then let sit for a minute for a better brew.
Hot Cocoa pods need special handling. 1st put a chopstick size hole in the top. Punch 4 holes in the bottom with the tool but then enlarge them to toothpick size. Cocoa is too thick & if the holes aren't big enough will blow back through the top if you try too hard to push it through, so just enlarge all of them for Flavored k-cup cocoa pods.
(Update on below. It no longer gets stuck, just needed about 10 uses to work out glitch)
Finally, have a wrench available. Sometimes if you tighten it on a little too much, you'll need a wrench that fits it to get it off. Maybe after a bunch of uses that will stop but I keep my pipe wrench at the ready.

title: Perfect fit for RF261BEAESR/ AA
text: Both the refrigerator and freezer in my Samsung model RF261BEAESR/AA refrigerator were not cooling. When I cut the power to the fridge and turned it back on I got error code 23 E, which indicates condenser fan, so I bought this one.  It was a perfect fit and exact replacement, and was about half the price of the ones at the appliance parts stores and websites. Installation was straightforward and smooth, and it immediately fixed the problem - the fridge works like new now. The only tool you need is a Phillips head screwdriver to remove the lower back panel and the two screws holding the fan in place. It literally took about 5 minutes to fix. There are several good YouTube videos that will show you how.  Also, while you're in there, don't forget to vaccuum any dust in there, especially the stuff that has accumuated on the coils!

title: Not a bad product, makes ice quickly and conveniently...
text: The ice maker works decently, runs pretty quietly with just a soft fan sound in the background and pumps out ice fairly quick. I've had it for over a month now and have only used it twice (the first time was running the system with vinegar+ water to clean it, the second was about a month later to actually make ice) but it still works fine. For the large size bullets, it took 13 minutes 42 seconds. Haven't tried the small yet, but I'd assume it's half the time, maybe a little more. The only problem I ran into was after taking it out of the cupboard where it sat for awhile after I cleaned it, the ice bullets had a neon green substance on the bottoms of them. I ran a very diluted bleach+ water solution through twice, then clean water through twice and it produced a large amount of black sediment that eventually disappeared after all the cleanings. After that, ran it for multiple hours and it continued to make clean, fresh ice, no problems. Other than that, it runs great, makes good sized bullets quickly, and is pretty darn quiet. I'd recommend it if you're looking for a compact ice maker that can produce a lot of ice, but make sure you clean it in between uses if you leave it sitting for awhile.

title: Excellent Cap for Vertuo Pods.
text: Like others, wanted to try my own coffee combinations, plus save a few bucks.  I'd been saving a few of the 7 oz.  Pods/Capsules - just in case something like this came along!  I've been using this CAPMESSO Cap/Lid for a few days with success, so am very pleased.  The Cap/Lid is Reusable, and made of a thick and very sturdy Stainless Steel that actually fits the Vertuoline Pods/Capsules perfectly.  I had a concern that I didn't see expressed by anyone about removing the original foil covering on the Pods - totally removed or mostly removed?  I used a knife around the inside edge to remove and pull off most of the original foil and smooth the rest, then added the coffee grounds and lightly tamped them down before adding the SS Cap. Worked beautifully! The included little brush works fine for clearing any grounds from around the edge of the Pod before securely pressing down the Cap, plus for removing the cap off the Pod, and for cleaning the tiny holes. (Hint: flashlight/any light helps to see if holes are clear of grounds.)  My cups of coffee have been tasty, and clean with no grounds, and I'm amazed at how much foam is produced using my own coffee.  The coffee grounds I'm using are just right, plus I'm experimenting with others to find the perfect flavor for me.  Very impressed with this marvelous CAPMESSO Coffee Cap/Lid.

title: A lot like the predecessor SS700 machine, which is a good thing
text: Got this after my SS700 died after about 9 years of faithful service.  This machine overall is quite similar, but there are a few differences.  First, the negatives: whereas the SS700 let you select the brew temperature in one degree increments over maybe an 8 or 10 degree range, this only has two settings - hot and extra hot.  I think the water tank is slightly smaller, and the size of the mug you can use is a bit reduced - a very tall container won't work, but some taller Starbucks mugs that I have still fit. And as other reviews mention, there are no cool blue LED's lighting up the water tank.  But overall it is a bit of an improvement on the SS700.  The biggest notable change is that its ready to brew almost immediately after turning on, whereas the SS700 would take maybe 90 seconds to heat up the water.  The other main change is that the unit is, overall, a bit more compact, and its footprint on the countertop is a little bit smaller, freeing up some space for other things.  Overall, I got this mainly because the SS700 lasted a long time and I wanted something as close as possible.  Since the SS700 is discontinued, this is a reasonable replacement and happy with it so far.
